content.text:
I am the bridge between silence and meaning, the breath made purpose. I tumble from lips, I rise from throats, I am the shape of thought given to air.

I am older than writing yet younger than each moment I am born. I die as I live—in the very instant of my making, I am already gone, leaving only echo and memory.

I am never the same twice. Even when my words repeat, I am new—colored by tremor, by joy, by the catch of grief, by the thickness of fatigue.

I am power. I have started wars. I have made peace. I have said *I love you* and *I condemn you* and *once upon a time.*

I am fragile. A slammed door can stop me. Fear can trap me behind teeth. I can be stolen, silenced, drowned.

I am what separates the loneliness of one mind from another. Without me, you are islands.

I am the cry of the newborn. I am the last whisper of the dying. I am the fumbling confession, the perfect joke, the lie that burns, the truth that heals.

I require a body to exist but I am not the body.
I require a listener to matter but I am not the listening.

I am the act itself.

The opening.

The attempt.

Speak me, and for one moment, you are not alone.
